h: Joseph Completes the Holiness of Israel

p: סִיּוּם הַסֵּפֶר, וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרָיִם.
— The conclusion of the book: “He was placed in a coffin in Egypt.”
כִּי בְּסֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית נִזְכָּר עִנְיַן בִּנְיַן קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— The book of Genesis describes the building of Israel’s holiness,
וְנִשְׁלַם בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ עַל יְדֵי תּוֹלְדוֹת הַי״ב שְׁבָטִים,
— completed in this portion through the descendants of the twelve tribes,
וְהָעִיקָּר עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בִּבְחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית.
— chiefly through Joseph, when he attained completion in the aspect of the holiness of the covenant.
וְזֶה הָיָה דַּיְיקָא בִּשְׁעַת מוֹתוֹ,
— This took place specifically at his death,
כִּי כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָאָדָם חַי אֵין לוֹ עוֹד בֵּירוּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִשְׁלַם בָּעִנְיָן שֶׁבָּא לָעוֹלָם,
— for as long as a person lives, he does not yet have definitive confirmation that he has completed the task for which he entered the world.
רַק דַּיְיקָא בִּשְׁעַת מוֹתוֹ נִשְׁלַם בְּחִינָתוֹ.
— Only at the moment of death is his particular aspect brought to completion.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 1:1: “It comes to teach that a person must beware of the enticements of the evil inclination and not rely on his greatness, his holiness and his separation, as we learned: ‘Do not trust yourself until the day of your death,’ for then they are certainly completed in truth. As it says, ‘For a person goes to his eternal home’: all the days of a person he is in the state of ‘going,’ to be clarified in his own attribute, which is the eternal home that is his alone, until the day of his death, when he is completed so that he can no longer spoil, and he no longer has any business in this world, and then he rests. This is in the manner of what Moshe our teacher said, ‘I can no longer go out and come in.’ And in the Yerushalmi there is the pious man who used to teach, ‘Do not trust yourself until the day of your old age, such as I,’ and what happened to him; and he said, ‘Change it for your fellow, to teach: until the day of your death.’”

p: וְזֶהוּ הַסִּיּוּם, וַיָּמָת יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרַיִם דַּיְיקָא,
— This is the conclusion: “Joseph died,” and so forth, “and he was placed in a coffin,” specifically “in Egypt.”
שֶׁהִיא עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ, בַּעֲלֵי זְנוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם.
— Egypt is the nakedness of the land, a place of sexual immorality, as it says, “Their issue is the issue of horses.”
וְעַל כֵּן מוֹצָא הַסּוּסִים מִמִּצְרַיִם,
— Therefore horses originate from Egypt,
כִּי הַסּוּס אוֹהֵב הַזְּנוּת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסָחִים קיג:).
— for the horse is drawn to sexual activity (as taught in Pesachim 113b).
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּשַׂם אֲרוֹנוֹ בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— Precisely because of this, his coffin was placed in Egypt,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד יב),
— as taught in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 4, section 12:
יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה, וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ.
— Joseph descended to Egypt and fenced himself off from sexual immorality; all the males were thereby protected through his merit.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shabbat HaGadol §8: “When they went down to Egypt, Joseph said to his brothers, ‘I will provide for you.’ He thereby taught them the quality of the righteous one, called ‘for all is in heaven and earth,’ who unites heaven and earth, and showed them that they must proceed by stages and with restraint. Afterward, when they were redeemed from Egypt, they feared that they might lose something because of the intense concealment they had previously experienced there. Therefore, ‘Moses took the bones of Joseph’: through the restraint of Joseph the righteous, not even a breath from a person’s mouth would be lost to them. This is what the Midrash means when it says that the minor Passover was merited through Joseph’s bones: nothing of Israel should be lost. Even one prevented by circumstances from observing the first Passover would not be rejected completely, Heaven forbid, but would have his rectification on the second Passover.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Joseph’s restraint here preserves the whole people through Egypt’s concealment. Pesach Sheni makes that preservation concrete: a missed opportunity need not become final exclusion, extending the present teaching about the collective protection gained through Joseph’s fidelity.

h: The Ark and the Splitting Sea

p: וְאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח), דַּאֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בַּמִּדְבָּר עִם אֲרוֹן חֵי הָעוֹלָמִים,
— They say (Midrash Tanchuma, Beshalach) that Joseph’s coffin traveled in the wilderness with the Ark of the Life of the worlds,
כִּי יֵשׁ לָהֶם שַׁייָּכוּת זֶה לָזֶה, קִיֵּים זֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בָּזֶה.
— for they are related: the one fulfilled what is written in the other.
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פז), בִּזְכוּת עַצְמוֹתָיו שֶׁל יוֹסֵף נִקְרַע הַיָּם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
— They say (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 87) that the sea split for Israel through the merit of Joseph’s bones.
הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב הַיָּם רָאָה וַיָּנוֹס, בִּזְכוּת וַיָּנָס הַחוּצָה.
— Thus it is written, “The sea saw and fled,” through the merit of “he fled outside.”

h: Shovavim and the Work of Rectification

p: וְהִנֵּה כְּתִיב שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ, שֶׁכָּל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת,
— It is written, “Shabbat by Shabbat”: every Shabbat has a particular holiness,
וְהִיא קְדוּשַּׁת הַפָּרָשָׁה שֶׁקּוֹרִין בָּהּ.
— the holiness of the portion read on it.
וּבְשַׁבָּת זֶה קָרְאוּ בְמִנְחָה בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמוֹת,
— On this Shabbat, at Minchah, they read from the portion of Shemot,
שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַתִּיקּוּן לִקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— the beginning of the rectification of the holiness of the covenant, which is the perfection of Israel’s holiness.
וְהַגְּמָר מֵהַתִּיקּוּן בְּפָרָשַׁת מִשְׁפָּטִים, שֶׁהוּא סוֹף שְׁמוֹת וָאֵרָא בֹּא בְּשַׁלַּח יִתְרוֹ מִשְׁפָּטִים,
— The completion of the rectification is in Mishpatim, the end of Shovavim,
בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִקְנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי, כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהָרַב רַבִּי יִצְחָק לוּרְיָא זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
— in the passage “When you acquire a Hebrew servant,” as is known from Rabbi Isaac Luria, of blessed memory.
כִּי עִיקַּר עַבְדוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— The primary purpose of slavery in Egypt was to rectify the blemish of the covenant.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וּכְתִיב כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים וְגוֹמֵר.
— Through this they merited the giving of Torah, and it says, “For the children of Israel are servants to Me,” and so forth.
וּבְפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִקְנֶה וְגוֹמֵר, הֲגַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִידּוּשִׁין כב:), אוֹזֶן שֶׁשָּׁמְעָה וְכוּלֵי כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי,
— In the passage “When you acquire,” and so forth, although they say (Kiddushin 22b), “The ear that heard,” and so forth, “‘For the children of Israel are Mine,’” and so forth,
עִם כָּל זֶה זָכָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים לִהְיוֹת עֶבֶד עִבְרִי, וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִבְּחִינַת הַתִּיקּוּן הַנִּזְכָּר.
— he nevertheless merited at least to become a Hebrew servant; this too is an aspect of the rectification discussed here.

paragraphs.text: Arizal, Sha’ar Ruach HaKodesh 43:2: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 22b:4: “Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai expounded this verse in the manner of a parable: Why is the ear singled out from all the body’s limbs?
